title: Production KPI Definitions, Denominators and Trend Interpretation

content.overview: A KPI is only as meaningful as its definition. Technician II records the eligible population, numerator, denominator, time window and exclusions before calculation, then compares like with like across cycles. One-cycle movement is a signal to investigate, not automatic proof of process improvement or decline.

vocabulary.definition: The defined eligible population or opportunity count used as the base of a rate or percentage.
The controlled statement of numerator, denominator, time window, unit and inclusion/exclusion rules for a metric.
A recurring direction or pattern across comparable observations rather than a single isolated value.

sections.title: Use the provided denominator exactly
sections.body: If a metric is defined as rooted units divided by eligible starting cuttings, discarded failures cannot be removed from the denominator unless the definition contains a documented exclusion rule.

sections.title: Compare only compatible definitions and windows
sections.body: A rate calculated from different eligibility rules or time windows is not directly comparable even if both are labeled with the same KPI name.

sections.title: One cycle is context, not a trend
sections.body: Use repeated comparable periods, planned-versus-actual context and known operational changes before treating a metric movement as a stable process signal.

workedExamples: A rooting KPI improves after failed units were excluded from the denominator; the apparent improvement is invalid until calculated under the original definition.
Harvest throughput drops in one cycle during an equipment outage; record the value and context rather than declaring a long-term decline.
commonMistakes: Changing the denominator after seeing the result.
Comparing metrics with different windows or eligibility rules.
Calling a single cycle a trend.
Using a KPI result without its definition and source records.
content.practicalApplication: Calculate three provided KPIs, write the numerator/denominator/time window beside each, then compare multiple cycles and identify which apparent changes are truly comparable.
content.summary: Correct KPI reasoning begins with stable definitions and ends with cautious, context-aware trend interpretation.
